newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-KANSAS CITY WIZARDS RALLY, WIN SHOOTOUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-KANSAS CITY WIZARDS RALLY, WIN SHOOTOUT.

text.p: Preki created two goals in regulation and converted the game-winning shootout goal to lift the Kansas City Wizards to a wild 4-3 victory over the New York/New Jersey MetroStars in Major League Soccer action on Sunday.

Mark Chung's goal with seven minutes remaining forced the shootout, which was won by the Wizards (17-7), 2-0. Chung also scored in the tie-breaker as goalkeeper Mike Ammann made three saves and forced a fourth attempt wide left. Former U.S. international forward Frank Klopas also had a goal in regulation.

Giovanni Savarese, who left immediately after the game to join his Venezuelan teammates for a World Cup qualifying match against Peru on Wednesday, scored twice for the MetroStars (7-15). Former Italian international Roberto Donadoni converted a penalty kick. U.S. National Team midfielder Tab Ramos was red carded in the 41st minute for arguing with the referee.

In Pasadena, California, the San Jose Clash (10-16) recorded its third consecutive win with a 3-2 triumph over the Los Angeles Galaxy (10-14) as Jeff Baicher scored twice in the opening half. Lawrence Lozzano also scored for the winners as Ronald Cerritos tied the league record by extending his point streak to 10 games.
Guatemalan Martin Machon and El Salvadoran Mauricio Cienfuegos had goals for the Galaxy.
In other action over the weekend:

In Denver, Wolde Harris, the MLS player of the week, scored one goal and set up the second as the Colorado Rapids (13-12) defeated the MetroStars, 2-0. Harris converted a penalty kick after Brazilian World Cup hero and defender Branco fouled U.S. international Marcelo Balboa in the penalty area and created Ross Paule's goal in the waning minutes.
Branco was later red carded for tackling Harris from behind.

In Tampa, Roy Lassiter and Sam George, acquired only days prior in a four-player trade with the New England Revolution to give the Tampa Bay Mutiny (14-11) a 2-1 win over the Dallas Burn (12-12). The Mutiny have a league-best 10-2 home record. Jason Kreis scored for the Burn, which have lost three straight games.

In Columbus, Ohio, U.S. national team goalkeeper Brad Friedel made six saves as he and the Columbus Crew (10-14) blanked D.C. United (16-9), the MLS's high scoring team, 2-0. It was Friedel's fifth shutout of the season.
U.S. international Thomas Dooley and Pete Marino scored four minutes apart midway through the second half. Crew coach Tom Fitzgerald was red carded in the 19th minute for arguing with the referee.

United, which entered the match with 54 goals, played without midfielder Marco Etcheverry and forward Jaime Moreno, the MLS co-scoring leader, who are in Bolivia preparing for Wednesday's World Cup qualifier.

In Foxboro, Massachusetts, the Galaxy withstood a game-tying goal in the 90th minute to upend New England (12-12) in a shootout, 2-1. Regulation ended in a 1-1 tie after Ivan McKinley, acquired in the Tampa trade, equalized with 25 seconds remaining. The loss was the Revolution's fifth consecutive defeat.

Chris Armas, U.S. international Cobi Jones and Machon converted their attempts in the tie-breaker while Mexican goalkeeper Jorge Campos made one save. Former Revolution midfielder Welton scored for the Galaxy.
